keyFindings.description: The body carried no `## Contract change census` for the required `heldOutboxRows` member of the strict `LegionStateResponse`, the `record.Store` changes (`ClaimDue` removed; `HeldRows`/`ExpediteOutbox` signatures) and `runtime.Runtime.LaunchBound()`; the implementer added it as a body edit at this head on request, and its rows match the reviewer's own searches (every parser migrated; no `ClaimDue`, `outboxPoll` or `outboxBatchSize` survivor; every `legion state` reader in `scripts/` uses `--json`). Resolved in the body before the review was submitted.

Three comments say an issue's lifecycle rows run "in the order they were queued"; the lanes run them oldest due first (plan §9.2, `outbox_lanes.go:17`, troubleshooting.md), and a backing-off suspend is passed by a due removal. Nothing relies on queue order (`removeWorkspace` guards on retired claims itself). Wording; fast-follow.

`Run` reuses a non-nil lanes map and a lane's `ctx.Done()` exits do not delete their entry, so a second `Run` on one `outbox` would nudge dead channels. Latent: `Run` is called once per process (`workflow.go:509`) and once per runner in every test. Fast-follow: assign a fresh map in `Run`.

The detached settle is chosen by a point-in-time `ctx.Err()` check, and the renewal tick's goroutine is outside the WaitGroup. A cancel landing between the check and the settle's transaction leaves the row leased until the sweep (the pre-change behaviour on every stop); a straggling tick is fenced by the lease token and records nothing. Fast-follow: always settle on the detached context.

A daemon stop now records the interrupted row's retry (`attempts + 1`, `last_error = context canceled`) where the old runner recorded nothing; the row's next run is one capped backoff later and `pendingStatusWrites[].lastError` reads the cancellation until then. Plan D6's design, pinned by `TestRunReturnsOnlyAfterItsLanesAndSettlesTheRowAStopInterrupted`; recorded in the body's Not proven / risk.

`runtime.Runtime.LaunchBound()` is implemented three times and read by no production caller (the Sandbox runtime applies its private `launchBound` at `relaunch.go:104`). Fast-follow: give it a reader or drop it from the interface.

A kind missing from `laneKinds` would be classified board by `UnfinishedLanes` yet excluded by the board lane's list (stranded on the sweep path), or reach `DueRows` with nil kinds, which lists every kind (over-listed on the wake path), silently. Every kind is registered today (`TestEveryOutboxKindIsInExactlyOneLane`). Fast-follow: key the table by kind and have `DueRows` refuse an empty kinds list.

`store.go` is 1045 lines with a self-contained outbox block; `HeldRows` carries the tautological `not (outboxClaimable)` conjunct to bind shared parameters (the body's existing Fast-follow); 0043's comment declares `outbox_due` unused but leaves it. Fast-follow.
`legion state`'s help text does not name the new `held lifecycle rows` line. Fast-follow.
